title: Fixed-thickening completion reflects a quantitative coherent kernel torsion bound
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], $I,K$ quasi-coherent ideal sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-closed-subscheme], and $q,s\geq1$. Put $Z=V(K^q)$. Assume for every Noetherian instance on $Z$ that completion with respect to $I\mathcal O_Z$ [def-nagata-extended-ideal] is an equivalence. Let $F,G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $a:F\to G$ a morphism [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Assume $K^qF=K^qG=0$. If for every $n\geq0$ the ordinary sheaf kernel and cokernel of $a\bmod I^{n+1}:F/I^{n+1}F\to G/I^{n+1}G$ are killed by $K^s$, then $K^{2s}$ kills the ordinary sheaf kernel of $a$. Ideal products and reductions have their shared image/cokernel definitions [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module].

source.place: Tag 088A (lemma-existence-tricky), second application of Remark 0888 (remark-inverse-systems-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-by), bound K^(4t); verified at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/088A and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0888

proof.text: Put Z=V(K^q). Its closed immersion into the Noetherian scheme X has Noetherian source. The coherent closed-pushforward equivalence descends F,G,a to Z. Its natural completion comparison and the ideal-power pushforward comparison transfer the component bounds to the completion of this descended map with respect to I O_Z, using the ideal K O_Z.

Apply the fixed-exponent affine-limit annihilation statement to the descended completed map. On each affine of Z, the s-th power kills every component kernel and cokernel, so the 2s-th power kills the kernel of the inverse-limit map. The affine formal-module equivalence identifies this with the kernel of the completed map.

Completion of finite modules is naturally tensoring with the completed ring, which is flat. Thus it preserves the kernel of the descended coherent map and the image of the ideal-action map on that kernel. The affine ideal-product calculation identifies the completed image with the product by the extended 2s-th ideal power, which is zero by the preceding bound. Therefore the completion of this coherent product is zero on every affine and hence globally.

The assumed global completion equivalence on Z reflects zero objects, so the coherent product itself is zero. Exact closed pushforward identifies the descended kernel with the ordinary sheaf kernel of a; its ideal-power comparison identifies the zero product with K^(2s) kernel(a) on X.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentMap_completion_torsion_kernel_reflection
    {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (q : ℕ) (hq : 1 ≤ q)
    (hcompletion : ∀ (hZ : IsNoetherian (K ^ q).subscheme),
      Functor.IsEquivalence
        (@completion ((K ^ q).subscheme) hZ (I.comap (K ^ q).subschemeι)))
    (F G : CoherentModules X) (a : F ⟶ G)
    (hF : IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι q).2 F.obj))
    (hG : IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι q).2 G.obj))
    (s : ℕ) (hs : 1 ≤ s)
    (h : ∀ n : ℕ,
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι s).2
        (kernel (formalModuleQuotientMap I a.hom (Nat.le_refl (n + 1))))) ∧
      IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι s).2
        (cokernel (formalModuleQuotientMap I a.hom (Nat.le_refl (n + 1)))))) :
    IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower K.toModulesι (2 * s)).2
      (kernel a.hom))
